record.paper_title: Some open questions on morphological operators and representations in the deep learning era: A personal vision
record.original_question: What Lipschitz morphological layers can be introduced into deep neural networks to control their Lipschitz constants and regularity, and can these morphological regularizing layers replace standard nonlinearities such as pooling plus ReLU without degrading network expressiveness?

evidence.quote: What kind of Lipschitz morphological layers can be introduced into deep networks to control their Lipschitz constant and therefore their regularity? Can these morphological regularizing layers replace the standard nonlinearities like pooling+ReLU without degrading their expressiveness?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. Mathematical morphology on grayscale images is built from two basic nonlinear operators acting on a function f : R^d → R with respect to a structuring function b : R^d → R ∪ {−∞}: the dilation (f ⊕ b)(x) = sup_{y ∈ R^d} { f(x − y) + b(y) } and the erosion (f ⊖ b)(x) = inf_{y ∈ R^d} { f(x + y) − b(y) }. A flat structuring element on a compact set B ⊂ R^d corresponds to b = 0 on B and −∞ elsewhere, recovering the local sup/inf operators. A map T between normed function spaces is L-Lipschitz if ||T(f) − T(g)|| ≤ L · ||f − g|| for all f, g.

A feed-forward neural network is a composition F = L_n ∘ σ_{n−1} ∘ L_{n−1} ∘ ··· ∘ σ_1 ∘ L_1, where each L_k is an affine (or convolutional) operator and each σ_k is a pointwise nonlinearity (e.g. ReLU x ↦ max(x,0)) possibly followed by a pooling operator (e.g. max-pooling). The Lipschitz constant of F (with respect to specified input/output norms) is bounded above by the product of the Lipschitz constants of its layers, and controls the regularity, robustness and generalization of the network.

Define a "morphological layer" to be any layer M whose action on its input feature maps is given by a finite composition of dilations, erosions, openings (f ↦ (f ⊖ b) ⊕ b), closings (f ↦ (f ⊕ b) ⊖ b), or supremal/infimal convolutions with learnable structuring functions, possibly followed by an affine combination across channels.

Problem. 
(a) Characterize the families of morphological layers M as above for which one can give an explicit, sharp, computable upper bound on the Lipschitz constant Lip(M) (with respect to the L^∞ and L^2 norms on inputs and outputs), in terms of the parameters of the structuring functions; describe in particular which choices of structuring functions and channel-mixing rules guarantee Lip(M) ≤ 1.

(b) Determine whether such "Lipschitz morphological layers" can be inserted into a deep neural network so as to control its overall Lipschitz constant while preserving — or improving — the network's expressive power. Concretely: exhibit, or prove the impossibility of, an architecture in which every standard nonlinearity of the form (max-pooling ∘ ReLU) is replaced by a Lipschitz morphological layer, in such a way that the resulting class of functions is at least as expressive (in a precise approximation-theoretic sense, e.g. universal approximation on compact sets of continuous functions) as the original architecture.
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches show extensive ongoing work on (i) Lipschitz regularization of neural networks (spectral normalization, Lipschitz bounds for ReLU/max-pooling) and (ii) morphological neural networks based on learnable dilations/erosions. However, no source was found that provides a complete characterization of Lipschitz morphological layers replacing pooling+ReLU without loss of expressiveness; the question appears to remain an open research direction.

status_evidence.title: Lipschitz regularity of deep neural networks: analysis and efficient estimation
status_evidence.snippet: ReLU, max-pooling, and common activations have Lipschitz constant 1; bounds on full network Lipschitz constants are studied.
status_evidence.claim: Lipschitz analysis of standard layers is well developed but does not address morphological layers.

status_evidence.title: Deep Morphological Neural Networks
status_evidence.snippet: Morphological neural networks use learnable dilation/erosion layers as nonlinear feature extractors.
status_evidence.claim: Morphological layers are an active research topic but their Lipschitz control and expressiveness vs. pooling+ReLU remain unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Learning Grayscale Mathematical Morphology with Smooth Morphological Layers
status_evidence.snippet: Smooth approximations of morphological layers are studied for trainability.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work explores trainable morphological layers but does not give the sought Lipschitz/expressiveness equivalence.
